chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning

A man performed tayammum and prayed, then he found water. So he said: As for me, I would have done so; indeed I would perform wudu and repeat [the prayer]. The correct way to understand this report is that repetition is obligatory if he finds water while time still remains. But if he prayed at the end of the time and the time has departed, repetition is not required of him. And that which indicates this is what...

key_terms.الْوَقْتُ: the prescribed time of the prayer
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute for wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water before the prayer time ends, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of one who performed tayammum and then found water after salat. Its indicated meaning is that the prayer is repeated only if water is found while the prayer time still remains; if the time has passed, no repetition is required.
